title: Migration policy is being rebuilt as cross-domain infrastructure linking labor, demography, AI, climate, data, and social cohesion
source_unit: European Commission Directorate-General for Research and Innovation, Future research on migration, human mobility and integration: Opportunities and Needs
geography: European Union research and policy ecosystem, with relevance to migration, mobility, integration, labor markets, technology, climate, and social cohesion across Europe

denominator.unit: more than 100 representatives from EU projects, public administrations, international organizations, civil society, universities, and research organizations consulted

research_reframing.value: migration research is positioned as a cross-cutting enabler of competitiveness, demographic resilience, labor-market sustainability, innovation, and social cohesion

policy_orientation.value: consolidate, organize, and scale evidence so it can address long-term challenges more effectively

observations.method: European Commission synthesis of EU-funded migration research and a multi-stakeholder consultation process; this is an agenda-setting and research-infrastructure report, not a population survey or impact evaluation.
observations.uncertainty: The report identifies strategic priorities and evidence needs; it does not show that research coordination changes migration outcomes, labor markets, integration, or public attitudes.
observations.subgroup: Migrants, local authorities, employers, researchers, public agencies, civil-society organizations, policymakers, and communities affected by integration and mobility systems.
observations.counterinterpretation: Framing migration as a competitiveness or resilience resource can improve policy coordination but may instrumentalize migrants unless rights, belonging, participation, and non-economic outcomes remain explicit.

observations.period: 2026; strategic research priorities for migration and integration

denominator.unit: strategic areas identified for future European migration research

priority_areas.value: integration; labor-market sustainability and socioeconomic resilience; legal migration pathways; technology and AI; climate-related mobility; science-policy connection; shared data and infrastructure; and practical application of research

cross_domain_signal.value: migration is treated as connected to demographic change, labor demand, technological change, climate, and geopolitical instability

implementation_gap.value: the report emphasizes faster movement from research tools and tested solutions into operational programs

observations.method: Policy-priority synthesis based on consultation and review of EU-funded migration research.
observations.uncertainty: Priority inclusion does not establish funding, implementation, equal regional coverage, or successful operational transfer.
observations.subgroup: Research funders, national and local governments, migration and integration services, technology developers, labor-market institutions, and affected communities.
observations.counterinterpretation: A broad agenda can improve coordination but may diffuse accountability if no institution owns delivery, data standards, rights protection, or public feedback.

denominator.unit: collaborative migration projects supported by Horizon 2020 and Horizon Europe, as reported in the associated public summary

research_investment.unit: euros reported as support for the 52 collaborative projects

knowledge_infrastructure.value: the report calls for stronger consolidation, organization, shared data, and transfer of research outputs into practice

governance_bridge.value: researchers, public authorities, local actors, civil society, and migrants are expected to be connected more closely in future research design and use

observations.method: Program-level figures and recommendations reported in the EU publication ecosystem; not an evaluation of project quality, causal return, or distribution of funds.
observations.uncertainty: Project counts and investment totals describe research activity, not implementation results, migrant welfare, policy effectiveness, or public legitimacy.
observations.subgroup: EU research projects, funders, policy users, local governments, civil-society partners, and people affected by migration and integration policy.
observations.counterinterpretation: More research infrastructure may improve evidence but can also reproduce top-down agenda setting if migrant, local, and frontline knowledge is not given decision power.

integration_scope.value: integration is linked to labor-market sustainability, demographic resilience, innovation, climate mobility, technology, and social cohesion rather than treated as a standalone settlement service

anticipatory_orientation.value: the report calls for research able to anticipate demographic, labor, AI, climate, and geopolitical transformations

local_application.value: the research agenda emphasizes practical application and stronger connections between evidence producers and local or regional authorities

observations.method: European Commission policy and research-system synthesis.
observations.uncertainty: This is an institutional framing of future research needs, not evidence that integrated migration policy has already been implemented or produces better social outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Local and regional governments, migrants and host communities, labor and education systems, technology and data institutions, and research funders.
observations.counterinterpretation: Integrated framing can support joined-up policy, but it can also place migration inside competitiveness agendas that underweight rights, cultural belonging, or democratic participation.

related_sources.claim: Associated public summary describing the eight priorities, more than 100 participants, and reported project investment.
Official DOI for the European Commission publication.

boundary: This record adds a migration-policy research-capacity and systems-framing route. It is not a migrant survey, labor-market outcome study, integration evaluation, causal policy test, or proof that research coordination changes public attitudes or lived conditions.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official European Commission Publications Office metadata and associated public summary were reviewed; consultation process, eight strategic areas, cross-domain framing, research-to-practice emphasis, and investment-context claims were cross-checked.
